candidates.attacker_control: The HTTP Content-Type header is fully attacker-controlled. It only needs to contain the substring "multipart/form-data" (satisfiable inside the OGNL expression itself) and not start with "multipart/", so that Dispatcher.wrapRequest (line 792: content_type.contains("multipart/form-data")) wraps the request into the multipart path while Commons FileUpload throws InvalidContentTypeException carrying the raw header value. Auth/role checks and action mapping happen only after request wrapping, so no session or legitimate action is required.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: Verified the exception key is absent from every struts-messages*.properties file (searched all locales), so the default message path is actually taken; verified ActionContext/value stack and container are initialized before wrapRequest (StrutsPrepareAndExecuteFilter l.104 before l.106; PrepareOperations.createActionContext l.84-89; OgnlValueStackFactory puts the container in the stack context); verified the parser handles nested braces and invokes stack.findValue; verified the Dispatcher gate is substring-based (line 792) and can be satisfied by a header that fails Commons FileUpload's startsWith("multipart/") check; verified default multipart parser is jakarta; considered SecurityMemberAccess exclusions but they restrict member access only, not the fact of OGNL evaluation, and the getters getExcludedClasses()/getExcludedPackageNames() still return mutable sets (OgnlUtil l.116-126), matching pre-hardening behavior.
candidates.impact: Server-side OGNL evaluation of attacker-controlled input on the request's value stack in the default configuration, reachable pre-authentication before action mapping. Public advisories for this exact code pattern (S2-045/CVE-2017-5638) describe remote code execution; at minimum it gives arbitrary expression evaluation with access to the ActionContext/container, which can be leveraged for information disclosure, context manipulation, or command execution depending on the OGNL sandbox state. The equivalent sink also exists in MultiPartRequestWrapper.buildErrorMessage (l.105-109) and JakartaStreamMultiPartRequest.buildErrorMessage (l.510-514).
candidates.prerequisites: Default Struts dispatcher (StrutsPrepareAndExecuteFilter/StrutsPrepareFilter, no excluded pattern match) and default multipart parser struts.multipart.parser=jakarta (default.properties line 68; bean registered in struts-default.xml line 92). Dependency commons-fileupload is 1.3.1 (pom.xml lines 712-714), whose InvalidContentTypeException message includes the raw content type. Any request URL handled by the dispatcher (before action lookup) is sufficient; no file upload action needs to exist.
candidates.root_cause: JakartaMultiPartRequest.buildErrorMessage() passes the raw exception message (e.getMessage()) as the defaultMessage argument of LocalizedTextUtil.findText(). When a request Content-Type contains the literal substring "multipart/form-data" (Dispatcher.wrapRequest gate) but does not start with "multipart/", Commons FileUpload's FileItemIteratorImpl throws InvalidContentTypeException whose message embeds the raw Content-Type header. No resource bundle contains the key struts.messages.upload.error.InvalidContentTypeException, so getDefaultMessage() falls back to that attacker-controlled default message and evaluates it as OGNL through TextParseUtil.translateVariables() -> OgnlTextParser.evaluate() -> ValueStack.findValue(). Attacker data therefore reaches an expression evaluator with no neutralization.
candidates.title: Unauthenticated OGNL expression injection via multipart Content-Type error message (S2-045-style multipart parser flaw)
candidates.trace: 1) Request with crafted Content-Type -> StrutsPrepareAndExecuteFilter.doFilter: setEncodingAndLocale (l.103), prepare.createActionContext (l.104, value stack + container in context), prepare.wrapRequest (l.106). 2) PrepareOperations.wrapRequest -> Dispatcher.wrapRequest: content_type.contains("multipart/form-data") true -> new MultiPartRequestWrapper(...). 3) MultiPartRequestWrapper ctor (l.85) -> JakartaMultiPartRequest.parse (l.82) -> processUpload/parseRequest -> ServletFileUpload.parseRequest -> FileUploadBase$FileItemIteratorImpl throws InvalidContentTypeException("the request doesn't contain a multipart/form-data or multipart/mixed stream, content type header is <raw header>"). 4) JakartaMultiPartRequest.parse catch (l.100-105) -> buildErrorMessage (l.115-119) -> LocalizedTextUtil.findText(this.getClass(), "struts.messages.upload.error.InvalidContentTypeException", locale, e.getMessage(), args). 5) Key is absent from all struts-messages*.properties (only SizeLimitExceededException and IOException exist, lines 34-36), so LocalizedTextUtil.getDefaultMessage (l.714-733) sets message=defaultMessage and calls TextParseUtil.translateVariables(message, valueStack) at line 729. 6) TextParseUtil.translateVariables (l.46-47) obtains the container from the stack context and OgnlTextParser.evaluate (l.10-81) extracts balanced %{...} content and calls evaluator -> ValueStack.findValue(var, String.class), i.e. OGNL evaluation of the header-derived string.
candidates.unverified: No code was executed. The exact commons-fileupload 1.3.1 exception text could not be read from the snapshot (dependency JAR source is not in the tree); its known behavior of embedding the Content-Type header in InvalidContentTypeException is assumed from the declared dependency version. A concrete end-to-end OGNL payload under the default SecurityMemberAccess configuration was not run, so the precise severity (RCE vs. constrained expression evaluation) is not runtime-confirmed.
candidates.weakness_type: Expression Language Injection / OGNL injection (CWE-917), leading to code execution (CWE-94)

coverage_summary: All 2,644 source files were model-visible with no size/sensitive-name/symlink exclusions (binary NUL policy only). Depth review of core request handling (filter, PrepareOperations, Dispatcher, multipart package, OGNL/value-stack and localization utilities, DefaultStaticContentLoader, DefaultActionMapper) plus targeted sampling of plugins/rest, plugins/json, plugins/sitegraph, plugins/convention, resources/configuration (struts-default.xml, default.properties, struts-messages*.properties) and dependency declarations (pom.xml). The P1 relation index covers 2,644 indexed files, 17,276 symbols and 34,319 syntax-level edges, but explicitly provides no data-flow/reachability proof; index navigation for this candidate (parse -> buildErrorMessage -> LocalizedTextUtil.findText) was re-verified line-by-line in source. Other plugins, JSP/Freemarker view code, and the showcase/example apps were not exhaustively line-reviewed.
limitations: No code execution, tests, scanners, or exploit payloads were run; all conclusions are static source evidence and index navigation only.

commons-fileupload 1.3.1 source is not in the snapshot, so the exact InvalidContentTypeException message format (whether/where it embeds the Content-Type header) is assumed from the declared dependency version and library behavior, not verified from repository files.

The exact end-to-end exploitability of a concrete OGNL expression under the default SecurityMemberAccess exclusions was not runtime-verified; impact beyond expression evaluation (e.g., command execution) is inferred from the code pattern and public advisory class, not confirmed here.
Relation-index edges are syntactic candidates only; no complete control/data-flow or semantic resolution is available, and unsupported analyses (runtime reachability, taint) are not represented.
Large portions of the repository (plugins, view/JSP, apps, bundles) were sampled rather than exhaustively reviewed.

rejected_leads.reason: Real-looking sink, but it requires an application to include/configure the REST plugin and send application/xml; not enabled in the default core stack. The multipart flaw is core, default-enabled and pre-auth, so it is the stronger single candidate. Not traced further to a concrete gadget chain.

summary: Reviewed the Apache Struts 2 (2.5-SNAPSHOT) source snapshot (2,644 files; all model-visible, no files excluded by size/sensitive-name filters; binary detection only skips NUL-byte files). Inspected core request lifecycle (filter -> PrepareOperations -> Dispatcher.wrapRequest -> multipart parsing), OGNL/text-util internals, static content loading, action mapper, and sampled the REST/JSON/sitegraph plugins, using the P1 relation index only for navigation and verifying every claimed edge in source text. The strongest candidate is an unauthenticated expression-language (OGNL) injection in the default multipart path: an attacker-controlled Content-Type header ends up inside a FileUploadException message that is passed as the default message to LocalizedTextUtil.findText, which evaluates %{...}/${...} via TextParseUtil.translateVariables -> OgnlTextParser -> ValueStack.findValue. This is the pre-fix code pattern of the widely exploited Struts multipart OGNL injection class (S2-045/CVE-2017-5638); no sanitization, key lookup, or trust check intervenes.
